main_text.p: præferri debet ligni & corticis Guaiaci de-coctum,cum tenuissimo uictu. Verùm his non utendum est, nisi ante purgato corpo-re.Tertia enim corporis regio,quàm habitum corporis dicimus,rectè expurgari nò poteft,nisi prima & fecunda, probè fuerint euacuatæ.Ad hæc etiam non parum confe runt offa combusta in pollinem redacta, & assumpta,& præsertim humana, quibus Galenus,libro Simplicium medicamentorû undecimo,uim admodum digerentem exiccantemque tribuit. Noui(inquit ille)no-ftratium quofdam offa potui exhibuiffe, haud scientibus quid'nam ebibiffent,ne ui delicet,auerfarentur,ac multorum, tum epilepfiam,tum arthritidè curaffe. Hæc Galenus,cuius authoritate, & sententia freti nó paucis arthriticis ofsium humanorum cinerem cum conferuis florum rofmarini, & betonicæ fœlicissimo fucceffu exhibuimus. Cornu item ceruinum, fiue crudum, fiue uftum læuigatum, & cum ijfdem conferuis fumptum non minus prodeffe fert. Superfluos enim humores corporis exiemiè confumit,ac digerit.Quòd ad arthriti-corum rationem uictus attinet, ea semper [?]sit tenuis oportet,ne gignendæ arthritidis pro-

page.notes: Lower-left corner of the text has a worn spot; the word "sit" at the start of the penultimate line is partly obscured by a blot, hence [?]. "fert" is read from a worn letter. Printed ornament at the lower left (a manicule-like mark) is not text. Running head ends in "NATVR." with the last letter partly worn; read as printed. No marginal notes on this page.
